Hi <@360491619402776577> I'm having trouble unmarshalling geth's `get_PayloadV2` reply with the block value. The spec says that it has to be a `QUANTITY 256bit`as such I expect the reply to be the handled on my end the same way as say `baseFeePerGas` which we unmarshal as a string. If I do treat them the same way, I can't produce any blocks. I get an error from the json unmarshaller. If I use insteafd of string `uint64` (which certainly should be the wrong type) my interop advances fine and I can propose blocks and withdraw and the such. I am not using blockvalue at all though. Yeah I think I made an oopsie with the marshalling I'll fix tomorrow I'll merge then unmarshalling as 64uint since I can't test nethermind yet (can't compile NET yet on arch) <@144468805697929216> I was using this command not long ago and it worked https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/1047873497432596501, now something similar tells me that I cannot use validator, and private-key at the same time. How do I specify a private key and request a BLS change for a given validator? have you tried to use the path? https://notes.ethereum.org/@bbusa/withdrawals#BLS-Change-to-execution-command-for-a-specific-validator-50 Here is an example I dion't have a mnemonic what do you mean by path? Oh. Is it for our network? I thought I sent you the mnemonic no, the devnet is not very useful since we are all following completely different specs, this is for interop, I want to test multiple withdrawals at the same time did ethdo lose the hability of creating a bls change from a privkey? `ethdo validator credentials set --validator=123 --withdrawal-address=0x8f…9F --private-key=0x3b…9c` this should still work it doesn't for me maybe you don't need to specify the --validator if you have different private keys for different validators. ``` potuz@forkchoice ~/Documents/code/ethereum/go-ethereum $ ethdo validator credentials set --validator=0 --withdrawal-address=0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 --private-key=0x25295f0d1d592a90b333e26e85149708208e9f8e8bc18f6c77bd62f8ad7a6866 --fork-version=0x20000092 --prepare-offline --genesis-validators-root=0xca5aaed5f2f3f6cba33396fbe60dfebfc3a5ea5bd03349b02db841cd35df1781 ``` That's the full command and I get ``` Error: failed to process: only one of validator, mmenomic or private key should be specified ``` yeah I think you need to remove the --validator then it doesn't work, it spits a whole list of changes, obviously it can't know for which validator is the change I am requesting it spits a list of validator credentials have you tried --offline instead of --prepare-offline? I think the --prepare-offline is just meant to pull data from beaconchain yep it complains that no validator is specified (without the `--validator`) and the same complain above when I include it I'll download an earlier version <@144468805697929216> same command ``` $ ethdo validator credentials set --validator=0 --withdrawal-address=0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 --private-key=0x25295f0d1d592a90b333e26e85149708208e9f8e8bc18f6c77bd62f8ad7a6866 --fork-version=0x20000092 --offline --genesis-validators-root=0xca5aaed5f2f3f6cba33396fbe60dfebfc3a5ea5bd03349b02db841cd35df1781 ``` segfaults on 1.26.1 Ok removing the offline and just using json produces a `credential_operations.json` which is what I need Our spec change pr merged about 16 hrs ago which would limit the scanning range https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/pull/6593 the other thing that would have changed is our endpoint for bls_to_execution now accepts arrays rather than single... but that's obv not going to split 🙂 could turn the sweep size off by making it basically the number of validators..... For the record the docker image `consensys/teku@sha256:288b258563b2e906d25df1905b6d08ecd6d11a2b2b188ed868c89755a1537b27` will give you a version before the bounded withdrawals went it. 🙂 This should be fixed in 1.26.5 (and yes if you supply private key it will work out the validator for you, hence not wanting the validator option as well).
